api.reason: Chose the rendered tag (span or div). The host of a custom element is one generic wrapper and the clipped box takes no room in the flow, so the tag has nothing to decide; aria-live and role go on the host.
Framework ref forwarding; the custom element is its own reference.

api.upstream: aria-*, role, id, data-*, event handlers (BaseProps pass-through)
api.reason: Native attributes and listeners on the host element; not component API.

differences.text: The clip block sits on an inner box (part=base) rather than on the host: the host stays a generic inline wrapper that can carry aria-live, role and id, and the box is 1px with clip-path inset(50%) instead of clip: rect(0,0,0,0) (widest support is met by both; clip-path is the current form).
The clip declarations are !important in the reset layer, so no author rule (host style, ::part(base), a later layer) can displace them; upstream had no className/style for the same reason.

core.visually-hidden.notes: Guides: [mwg:accessibility] the visually-hidden utility (clip, 1px, nowrap) and live regions; [mwg:accessible-web-components] the host stays a generic wrapper, semantics come from the author.
